 Pennsylvania Democratic Senator John Fetterman’s first official 2028 challenger is a Palestinian American writer with an opposing view on one of Fetterman’s top issues: Israel. Ahmed Moor announced his run for Senate in Pennsylvania on Monday. "My name is Ahmed Moor and I’m running for U.S. Senate here in PA (election 2028)," he wrote on X. "I’m running to end the war in Iran and to promote the dignity agenda: free healthcare, free childcare, and affordable housing. I’m calling for accountability for genocide, for ICE and for corruption. And finally, for the protection of our civil liberties in America." Tuesday’s midterm elections showed growing frustration with the United States’ relationship with Israel, fueled by the unpopular U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. President Donald Trump has suggested cutting off aid to Israel and Vice President JD Vance has partly blamed his party’s defeat on U.S.-Israel relations. The 42-year-old Philadelphia resident told The Philadelphia Inquirer newspaper, which first reported his candidacy, he was inspired to run because of corruption, the cost of living, constitutional authority, and foreign policy. "I’m not really running against Fetterman," the Gaza-born former international development worker told the Inquirer. "I’m running for good government. I’m running for the rule of law. I’m running because I believe in America. And I believe in our capacity for renewal. I believe in our capacity for redressing wrongs in our midst." Newsweek has contacted Moor's campaign and Fetterman's office for comment via email and is awaiting responses. Fetterman, whose term runs until January 3, 2029, has not said whether he will seek a second term, but some Democrats have made it clear they want him out of office. His seat is next up for election in November 2028. He has seen his approval ratings plummet and has grown increasingly isolated from the Democratic Party, largely because of his staunch support for Israel. Fetterman has also faced criticism from wings of his party for frequently splitting with Democrats on issues ranging from immigration to Israel to vote with Republicans in a closely divided Senate. This led to speculation that he might switch parties—something he has denied. However, Democrats’ blue wave in the midterms elections saw them win decisive control of the Senate. So, Fetterman has now lost the unique leverage he had in Washington. Fetterman also faced criticism from Democrats after The Wall Street Journal reported in September that he had little interest in doing the work of a senator, including routinely ducking meetings with constituents. Who Is Ahmed Moor? Moor is a writer who was born in the Rafah refugee camp in the Gaza Strip. He has written for The Washington Post, Los Angeles Times and other outlets and has co-edited a book, After Zionism: One State for Israel and Palestine. Moor moved with his family to Sudan, Sierra Leone, Haiti and Nepal before moving to the United States, according to a biography on the Paul and Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans. This is a foundation that provides funding for immigrants and children of immigrants pursuing graduate studies. Moor received a bachelor’s degree in political science from the University of Pennsylvania in 2006. He then received a master’s degree in public policy from Harvard University in 2013 after being awarded the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship. Moor founded a digital lending company based in Jordan in 2013 and was previously the company’s CEO. He resides in Philadelphia with his wife and three children, according to his Senate campaign website. On the page, he said the country that welcomed his family "wasn’t perfect, but it was a land of opportunity. It gave me a great education and a career in journalism and public policy. It’s where I bought a home in the heart of West Philly with my wife and three kids." Moor cited U.S. support for Israel and the Iran war among the reasons why he is running for Senate. "A few years ago, my birthplace was turned to rubble in a genocide funded by you and me, with the support of politicians on both sides of the aisle who can't find money for transit or removing asbestos from our schools," he said on the page. "It's the same story now in Iran. We’ve spent $90 billion on a war no American wants, driving up the price of diesel and making our groceries more expensive. "It’s clear the United States funds wars based on corruption and lies and has turned its back on its own people. We must make sure this never happens again. That’s why I’m running for U.S. Senate." Independent experts commissioned by the U.N. said in a recent report that Israel has continued to carry out a genocide against the Palestinian people even after a ceasefire agreement in Gaza. Israel has repeatedly denied accusations of genocide. Shapiro Says People ‘Lining Up’ to Oust Fetterman Pennsylvania’s Democratic Governor Josh Shapiro has said he thinks Fetterman will face "a robust primary challenge" should he decide to run for a second term. In an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday, Shapiro said he has "no idea" what Fetterman’s plans are. "The good people of Pennsylvania have just voted, and they don’t want people enabling Donald Trump anymore. They want real accountability for Trump," Shapiro added. "They want people who actually show up in their communities every day and do the hard work to make their lives better. And I think John’s got a lot of work to do to earn the trust of the people of Pennsylvania, to reearn the trust of the people of Pennsylvania. He’s got to show up. He should speak to the people of Pennsylvania about what his plans are." Asked if he thinks Fetterman should face a primary challenge, Shapiro said: "I think there’s going to be a robust primary challenge." He added: "There’s no question that people are lining up to run, and he has to decide if he’s going to run."
